items.name: Nile
items.fact: Often cited as the world’s longest river.
facts: Often cited as the world’s longest river.
Flows north through 11 countries.
Empties into the Mediterranean.

items.name: Senegal River
items.fact: Forms most of the Senegal–Mauritania border.
facts: Forms most of the Senegal–Mauritania border.
Empties into the Atlantic at Saint-Louis.

items.name: Blue Nile
facts: The Nile’s chief floodwater source.
Rises at Lake Tana in Ethiopia.

items.name: White Nile
facts: The longer Nile headstream.
Flows from the Great Lakes through South Sudan.

items.name: Chelif
facts: Longest river in Algeria.
Flows to the Mediterranean west of Algiers.

items.name: Lake Nasser
facts: Reservoir behind Aswan High Dam.
The Nile’s great lake in Egypt and Sudan.

items.name: Lake Chad
items.fact: Shallow African lake; size varies greatly.
facts: Shallow African lake; size varies greatly.
Shared by Chad, Cameroon, Niger, and Nigeria.

items.name: Lake Qarun
facts: Egypt’s largest natural lake.
In the Faiyum Oasis, west of the Nile.

items.name: Chott el Djerid
facts: Tunisia’s largest salt pan.
A seasonal lake of the Sahara’s northern edge.

items.name: Lake Manzala
items.fact: Largest of the Nile Delta lakes.
facts: Largest of the Nile Delta lakes.
A coastal lagoon on the Mediterranean.

items.name: Mediterranean Sea
items.fact: Sea north of the Maghreb and Egypt.
facts: Sea north of the Maghreb and Egypt.

items.name: Atlantic Ocean
items.fact: Ocean west of Morocco and Western Sahara.
facts: Ocean west of Morocco and Western Sahara.

items.name: Red Sea
items.fact: Sea east of Egypt and Sudan.
facts: Sea east of Egypt and Sudan.

items.name: Strait of Gibraltar
facts: Between Morocco and Spain.

items.name: Suez Canal
items.fact: Links the Mediterranean and the Red Sea.
facts: Links the Mediterranean and the Red Sea.

items.name: Gulf of Sidra
facts: Mediterranean gulf of Libya.
Also called the Gulf of Sirte.

items.name: Gulf of Gabès
facts: Mediterranean gulf of Tunisia.
